title: _claimRewards underflows and reverts after pauseWithdraw -> unpause -> claim sequence, bricking the user's reward-claim and normal withdraw paths
rootCause: `pauseWithdraw` decrements `user.amount` and `totalStaked` but does NOT rebase `user.phUSDDebt` / `user.stableDebt`. Subsequent `_claimRewards` computes `(user.amount * accX) / PRECISION - user.XDebt`; because `user.amount` was reduced while debts are anchored to the pre-pause amount, the new product can be strictly less than the stale debt, triggering Solidity 0.8 checked-subtraction underflow (Panic 0x11).

symbolic.claim: underflow reachable even with NO accumulator growth between pauseWithdraw and claim (broadens CODE-002 attackVector)
Halmos counterexample on the canonical 100e18 stake from CODE-002 attackVector

impactSummary: After legitimately recovering principal via `pauseWithdraw`, the user is permanently unable to call `claim`, `withdraw(amount < user.amount)`, or `stake(amount, recipient = victim)`: every path that reaches `_claimRewards` reverts. The user's only on-chain escape is another full `pauseWithdraw` during a future pause, which silently forfeits accrued rewards.
preservedDetails: CODE-002 carries the strongest narrative (full pre/post-condition walk-through, remediation menu). SYMBOLIC-001 broadens reachability beyond the profile §4.3 worked case. INV-01 provides a 5-step shrunk counterexample replayable in Foundry. SYMBOLIC-002 provides a canonical 100e18 witness for PoC generation.
remediation: Either (a) in `pauseWithdraw`, proportionally reduce `user.phUSDDebt`/`user.stableDebt` so `(user.amount * accX)/PRECISION >= user.XDebt` is preserved; or (b) clamp the subtraction in `_claimRewards`; or (c) call `_updatePool` + `_claimRewards` inside `pauseWithdraw` before the principal cut.
dedupNotes: INV-01 and SYMBOLIC-001/002 are evidence artefacts that PROMOTE CODE-002 from 'potential-high' to 'verified-high'. Carried forward as evidence links rather than separate findings. The shared underflow site is also reached from the view path, which is split into DEDUP-003 (CODE-007) because it has a distinct impact (front-end DoS vs mutating DoS) even though root cause is identical.
relatedFindings: DEDUP-011 (CODE-009 spec-level form: same root cause framed as forfeiture-without-event)
